title: Shell escape through a tool that passes an argument to a child process
prerequisites: a delegated command rule, SUID binary or scheduled job that runs the tool for you
the tool accepts an argument the parent does not sanitise
excerpt: Many Unix utilities delegate work to a child process or accept a command-shaped argument. When such a utility runs under a rule that grants more privilege than your own shell, the delegated child inherits that privilege. The technique is to find the delegation point, not to guess a payload: check the tool's manual for an option that names a program or an interpreter, then confirm which user the child ran as.
